59	      "page_level_design_instruction": "The BoltWorks Home page is a festival-poster landing experience built on a Voltage Black (#0D0D0D) base that never relents. The page reads like a concert program: loud, sequential, event-driven, with each section functioning as a distinct "lineup block" that alternates density and breathing room rather than repeating the same eyebrow→headline→CTA skeleton.

SECTION SEQUENCE & RHYTHM:
1. Hero — full-bleed, maximum amplitude, off-axis illustration overlapping into the viewport edge. Centered typographic stack but with a deliberate asymmetric illustration break.
2. Stats — a dense horizontal marquee-style band in Backstage Charcoal (#1E1E2A), oversized numerals as type-as-image, zero narrative copy — pure data as spectacle.
3. Feature Grid — 2×2 card grid on Voltage Black with top-edge color rules and tight lineup-block styling; moderate density with a clear CTA exit.
4. Timeline — a vertical spine layout with large date-badge nodes in Ignition Orange (#FF5C00) alternating left/right content blocks; the most editorial, highest-information section.
5. CTA Close — full-bleed Reactor Yellow (#FFE600) panel with a circuit-board pattern behind oversized black type; the loudest color moment on the page, a deliberate palette inversion.

SIGNATURE MOMENT:
The page's signature moment lives in the Hero (Section 1): the robot illustration is NOT contained inside a box or column — it bleeds off the right edge of the viewport and overlaps the stat band below, crossing the section boundary. The headline "BUILD. COMPETE. IGNITE." is set at 96px Archivo Black, fully uppercase, with ultra-tight tracking, split across three stacked lines where each word occupies its own line and the word "IGNITE." is stroked in Reactor Yellow (#FFE600) while the others are Crowd White (#FFFFFF). This multi-line stacked display headline with a single-word color punch, combined with the illustration bleeding past the section edge, is the unmistakable festival-poster typographic stunt that defines the page.

COLOR & SURFACE LOGIC:
- Sections 1, 3: Voltage Black (#0D0D0D) — the dominant dark stage floor.
- Section 2: Backstage Charcoal (#1E1E2A) — a subtle cool shift that creates depth without breaking the dark mood.
- Section 4: Voltage Black (#0D0D0D) with Ignition Orange (#FF5C00) structural nodes.
- Section 5: Full-bleed Reactor Yellow (#FFE600) — the single warm light surface, reserved for maximum contrast impact at the close.
Reactor Yellow is NOT only on buttons — it appears on the headline word "IGNITE." in the hero, on stat numeral highlights, and as the entire background of Section 5. Plasma Magenta (#FF1F8E) appears in the hero gradient overlay and on active/hover CTA states. Circuit Cyan (#00E5FF) appears as tag chips in the feature grid cards. Ignition Orange (#FF5C00) is structural — timeline nodes, card top-edge rules.

TYPOGRAPHIC HIERARCHY:
- H1 (Hero): Archivo Black, 96px, uppercase, tracking -0.03em, Crowd White + Reactor Yellow accent word.
- H2 (Stats, Feature Grid, Timeline, CTA): Archivo Black, 56–64px, uppercase, tracking -0.02em.
- H3 (Card/item titles): Archivo Black, 28–32px, uppercase.
- Eyebrows: Bebas Neue, 12px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.2em, Plasma Magenta or Circuit Cyan depending on surface.
- Body: Archivo Regular, 17px, 1.65 line-height, Poster Cream (#F5F0DC) on dark surfaces.
- Stat numerals: Archivo Black, 80–96px, Reactor Yellow on Backstage Charcoal — type-as-image treatment.
- Timeline date labels: Bebas Neue, 18px, uppercase, Ignition Orange.
- CTA Close headline: Archivo Black, 72–80px, uppercase, Voltage Black on Reactor Yellow.

DENSITY / WHITESPACE LOGIC:
The page alternates between high-density bands (Stats: zero whitespace, edge-to-edge numerals; Feature Grid: tight card gutters) and more open compositions (Timeline: generous vertical rhythm between nodes; Hero: tall viewport height with breathing room around the headline stack). This push-pull mirrors a festival program's alternation between packed lineup pages and full-bleed artist spreads.

Join the Club
GARAGE
Our Story

Born in a Garage.
Built for the World.

BoltWorks started with five kids, a pile of spare parts, and an unstoppable idea.

What began as an informal weekend tinkering group in 2016 has grown into one of the region's most celebrated youth robotics clubs — a place where every student, regardless of background or experience, gets a seat at the build table.

Mission & Values

We Build More
Than Robots

Our mission is to spark a lifelong love of engineering in every student who walks through our doors.

At BoltWorks, we believe the skills learned on the build floor — problem-solving, collaboration, resilience, and creative thinking — are the same skills that change the world. We don't just teach robotics. We build the next generation of engineers, innovators, and leaders.

Value 01

Curiosity First

We celebrate questions over answers and reward experimentation, even when the robot falls over.

Value 02

Every Builder Belongs

We actively recruit students from underrepresented communities and provide need-based scholarship access to all programs.

Value 03

Real-World Rigor

Our curriculum is designed with input from working engineers to ensure students learn skills that matter beyond the competition floor.

Value 04

Compete with Integrity

We train champions who win with grace, lose with dignity, and always help a rival team fix their robot before a match.

The Crew

Meet the People
Behind the Machines

Our coaches, mentors, and staff bring professional engineering experience and genuine enthusiasm to every session.

Director
DanaReyes

Former aerospace engineer and FRC alumna. Dana founded BoltWorks after seeing too many talented kids without access to quality STEM programs.

Build Coach
MarcusObi

Mechanical engineer with 10 years in robotics manufacturing. Marcus runs the fabrication floor and is famous for his "no bad ideas" brainstorm sessions.

Software Lead
PriyaNair

Software developer and CS educator who designed BoltWorks' three-tier coding curriculum, from Scratch to ROS.

Outreach
TomCallahan

Former high school teacher turned STEM advocate. Tom manages school partnerships, scholarship programs, and community demo events.

Contact Our Team
Our Impact

Numbers That Tell
The Real Story

Eight Years
8

Of continuous operation and growing community since our founding in 2016.

Alumni Path
40%

Of our alumni have gone on to pursue STEM degrees or careers.

Scholarships
$85K

In need-based scholarships distributed to members over the past three seasons.

Mentors
30+

Industry mentors and volunteer coaches who donate their time each season.

Join the Club
Find Your Stage

Every Builder
Has a Home
Here

BoltWorks is organized into specialized departments so every member can go deep on what they love most.

Whether you're drawn to the precision of mechanical design, the logic of code, the strategy of competition, or the art of communicating science — there's a department built for you.

DEPARTMENTS
Our Departments

Six Tracks. One Team.

Each department runs its own projects, workshops, and competitions — all feeding into the same championship robot.

Mechanical Engineering

Design and build the physical systems of the robot — chassis, drivetrain, manipulators, and structural components. CAD, prototyping, and fabrication are core skills.

Age 12–18 Beginner → Adv

Software & Controls

Write the code that makes the robot move, sense, and decide. Students work in Python, Java, and C++ using real robotics frameworks like WPILib and ROS.

Age 11–18 Beginner → Adv

Electrical & Wiring

Design the power systems, wire the motors and sensors, and ensure the robot's electronics are safe, reliable, and competition-ready.

Age 13–18 Intermediate+

Competition Strategy

Analyze opponents, plan match strategies, scout other teams, and make real-time tactical decisions during tournament play.

Age 10–18 All levels

Outreach & Communications

Tell the BoltWorks story to the world. Manage social media, write grant applications, organize community demos, and run our school ambassador program.

Age 10–18 All levels

Innovation Lab

A free-build sandbox for members who want to pursue independent robotics projects, enter external hackathons, or prototype ideas beyond the competition robot.

Age 8–18 All levels
Ask About a Department
Division Guide

Which Division Is
Right for You?

BoltWorks runs three age-based divisions, each with its own competition league and curriculum depth.

Sparks

Sparks Division

8–11

Introduction to robotics through LEGO Mindstorms and VEX IQ. Focus is on fun, exploration, and learning the basics of sensors and programming.

FormatWeekly 2-hour sessions
CompetitionJunior Robotics League
Voltage

Voltage Division

12–14

Intermediate builders working with VEX EDR and custom electronics. Teams design full robots for regional VEX competitions and internal BoltWorks tournaments.

Format2 sessions/week + weekend builds
CompetitionVEX Regional Circuit
Apex

Apex Division

15–18

The flagship program. Teams build full-scale competition robots for FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC). The most demanding and rewarding track BoltWorks offers.

Format3 sessions/week + intensive build
CompetitionFIRST Robotics (FRC)
Open Lab

Open Lab

All

Drop-in sessions for independent projects, skill workshops, and mentored free builds. No competition pressure — just making things.

FormatSaturday mornings
CompetitionNone — open exploration

Join the Club
The Innovation Stage

Student Engineers.
Real Research.
Serious Results.

BoltWorks members don't just build competition robots — they push the boundaries of what young engineers can achieve.

From autonomous navigation to computer vision and soft robotics, our research projects have been presented at regional science fairs, university symposia, and national STEM conferences. This is where curiosity becomes contribution.

Active Projects

What We're Building Right Now

Each project is student-led, mentor-supported, and aimed at solving a real engineering challenge.

Project ARIA — Autonomous Robot Intelligence Architecture

Active Apex + Voltage Lead: Priya Nair

A Voltage and Apex team collaboration developing a modular autonomous decision-making system using ROS2 and a custom sensor fusion pipeline. Goal: sub-3-second field mapping in FRC-scale environments.

SoftBot — Pneumatic Soft Robotics Gripper

Active Innovation Lab Lead: Marcus Obi

An Innovation Lab project exploring soft robotic actuators made from silicone molds and pneumatic control. The team is testing grip reliability on irregular game pieces.

VisionTrack — Real-Time Object Detection for FRC

Active Apex Lead: Aisha Mensah

A software team project implementing a YOLOv8 model trained on competition game pieces to enable real-time targeting and autonomous scoring. Achieved 94% detection accuracy in field tests.

EcoBot — Sustainable Materials in Robot Construction

Active Innovation Lab + Outreach Lead: Tom Callahan

An outreach-driven research project investigating the use of recycled and bio-based materials in robot chassis design. Partnered with a local university materials science lab.

DriveMetrics — Drivetrain Performance Analytics Dashboard

Completed Apex Lead: Carlos Rivera

A data engineering project that logs motor telemetry during practice matches and visualizes performance trends to guide mechanical tuning decisions.

of the Maker District

Our lab is accessible by public transit and has dedicated parking for weekend sessions.

BoltWorks is located at 240 Maker Street, Suite 4, Springfield, IL. We share a building with a local makerspace and a community workshop — the energy is contagious the moment you walk in.

240 Maker Street, Suite 4, Springfield, IL 62704
3:30–7:00 PM Weekdays | 9:00 AM–1:00 PM Saturdays
Quick Answers

Things People Usually Ask Us First

01 Does my child need prior experience to join? +

Absolutely not. Most of our members start with zero robotics experience. Our Sparks and Voltage divisions are designed specifically for complete beginners.

02 What does membership cost? +

Seasonal membership fees range from $150 to $350 depending on division. Need-based scholarships are available and cover up to 100% of fees. No student is turned away for financial reasons.

03 How do I enroll my child? +

Submit an enrollment inquiry through the contact form above. Our team will schedule a free orientation session where your child can meet coaches and try a build activity before committing.

04 Can businesses or individuals sponsor BoltWorks? +

Yes! Sponsorships start at $500 and include recognition on our competition robot, website, and event materials. Contact partners@boltworks.club for a sponsorship prospectus.

05 Do you partner with schools? +

We have formal partnerships with six schools in the region and offer in-school demo programs and teacher training. Contact Tom Callahan at outreach@boltworks.club to explore a partnership.

⚡ ⚡
One Last Thing

The Best Time to Join Was Last Season.
The Second Best Time Is Now.

Don't let another build season pass you by. The lab is warm, the mentors are ready, and there's a robot with your name on it.

Site built and ready at `/workspace/output/reference_site/`.

**What's there:**
- 5 pages — `index.html` (home), `about.html`, `departments.html`, `research.html`, `contact.html` — each with `data-page-slug` and 5 sections carrying the exact blueprint `id` and `data-section-type`.

- Home hero: stacked "Build. / Compete. / Ignite." with the yellow accent on the final word + bleeding robot illustration.
- About: rotated mega-word "GARAGE" pinned to the left edge.
- Departments: ghost-watermark "DEPARTMENTS" behind the 6-card grid + full-bleed yellow-band CTA headline.
- Research: full-bleed magenta→yellow gradient stats panel with oversized numerals.
- Contact: gradient form panel with overflowing 24-hours headline and the dual-bolt yellow finale.
